37:  */

39: let handlers = {
40:   parsers: {},
41:   formatters: {},
42:   validators: {}
43: }

45: export {MenqueryParam as Param}
46: export {MenquerySchema as Schema}

48: /**
49:  * Get or set a handler.
50:  * @param {string} type - Handler type.
51:  * @param {string} name - Handler name.
52:  * @param {Function} [fn] - Set the handler method.
53:  */
54: export function handler (type, name, fn) {
55:   if (arguments.length > 2) {
56:     handlers[type][name] = fn
57:   }
58: 
59:   return handlers[type][name]
60: }
61: 
62: /**
63:  * Get or set a parser.
64:  * @param {string} name - Parser name.
65:  * @param {parserFn} [fn] - Set the parser method.
66:  * @return {parserFn} The parser method.
67:  */
68: export function parser (name, fn) {
69:   return handler('parsers', ...arguments)
70: }
71: 
72: /**
73:  * Get or set a formatter.
74:  * @param {string} name - Formatter name.
75:  * @param {formatterFn} [fn] - Set the formatter method.
76:  * @return {formatterFn} The formatter method.
77:  */
78: export function formatter (name, fn) {
79:   return handler('formatters', ...arguments)
80: }
81: 
82: /**
83:  * Get or set a validator.
84:  * @param {string} name - Validator name.
85:  * @param {validatorFn} [fn] - Set the validator method.
86:  * @return {validatorFn} The validator method.
87:  */
88: export function validator (name, fn) {
89:   return handler('validators', ...arguments)
90: }
91: 
92: /**
93:  * Create a middleware.
94:  * @param {MenquerySchema|Object} [schema] - Schema object.
95:  * @param {Object} [options] - Options to be passed to schema.
96:  * @return {Function} The middleware.
97:  */
98: export function middleware (schema, options) {
99:   return function (req, res, next) {
100:     let _schema = schema instanceof MenquerySchema
101:                 ? _.clone(schema)
102:                 : new MenquerySchema(schema, options)
103: 
104:     _.forIn(handlers, (typedHandler, type) => {
105:       _.forIn(typedHandler, (handler, name) => {
106:         _schema.handler(type, name, handler)
107:       })
108:     })
109: 
110:     _schema.validate(req.query, (err) => {
111:       if (err) {
112:         res.status(400)
113:         return next(err)
114:       }
115: 
116:       req = _.merge(req, _schema.parse())
117:       next()
118:     })
119:   }
120: }
121: 
122: export default middleware

exact_cwe_mechanism.evidence: The candidate propagates globally registered handler functions to a schema instance. While this enables custom code execution on user input, CWE-94 specifically requires constructing/modifying code segments using external input. The evidence shows handler registration and execution, not code generation or modification.

connection.evidence: User-controlled req.query values flow to _schema.validate() and _schema.parse(), which invoke registered handlers (parsers, formatters, validators) that process parameter values. The candidate connects global handlers to the schema that processes user input.

diff_causality.evidence: If the candidate line were reverted, globally registered handlers would not be propagated to the schema instance during middleware initialization. Custom handlers would not execute on user-controlled query parameters, preventing the potential execution path.

security_control.evidence: The code shows schema.validate() occurs before parsing, but custom handlers can bypass or weaken built-in validation. No evidence of sandboxing, allowlisting, or validation of handler functions themselves.
security_control.required_control: Validation/sanitization of handler functions and their execution context
security_control.control_requirement_evidence: For CWE-94, code injection requires that externally-influenced input modifies code behavior. Here, handlers are functions that execute on user input, so controls must validate handler safety and sandbox execution.

No validation of globally registered handler functions

cwe_assessments.review_comment: The middleware propagates globally registered handler functions to schema instances that process user-controlled query parameters. Custom parsers, formatters, and validators execute on untrusted input without validation of handler safety.
